This turn closed the final quiesce gap.

**Observer under quiesce (new coverage, passes)**

`TestAuditObserverReadAndProposeAfterQuiesce` adds an observer to a quiesced two-voter cluster, then reads and proposes through it. All three nodes log `exited from quiesce, msg type ReadIndex`, the observer's read returns the expected state, and its proposal is visible from the other voter — so the non-voting path wakes the cluster correctly. (My first run of this test failed on my own bug: I reused the observer test's `PST` state machine, whose `Lookup` returns `[]byte`, then asserted `uint64`. Switching to the counter state machine fixed it; nothing in the product was implicated.)

**Report state**

- F13 section now covers idle reads, proposals, snapshots, membership changes, observers and leader loss; witness nodes need no check because they reject reads and proposals by design (`ErrInvalidOperation`).
- Inventory lists all three quiesce test files.
- "Unresolved work" no longer carries a quiesce caveat.
- Matrix updated to 43 audit tests (28 passing, 15 deliberate repro failures), root package at 25 tests.
- The fixed copy passes all quiesce tests together (`-run Quiesce`, 18.2 s), including the F13 repro that fails on the captured tree.

The audited implementation remains byte-identical to `../source`; everything added this turn is build-tagged test code plus report text.
